heading: The week in short
body: Two big releases are landing in November: Pokémon's Règne Delta on Friday 6 November, and One Piece's OP-18 from 20 November. Meanwhile the 30th Celebration cards keep sliding after their launch hype, and One Piece's Green Mihawk leader has been banned. For a collector, the window to buy 30th Celebration cards cheaply is open, while the new sets are best watched for a week or two after release before paying top prices for singles.

heading: Règne Delta lands Friday
body:
Méga-Évolution – Règne Delta (Delta Reign in English) releases worldwide on Friday 6 November. The headline card is Mega Rayquaza ex, the first Mega Rayquaza since the XY era, in a special illustration rare and a Mega Hyper Rare. Mega Golurk, Mega Malamar and Mega Golisopod ex round out the set, along with 6 special illustration rares and a new kind of card: Legendary Stadiums, pairs of stadiums that join into one picture.

Displays (36 packs) are on pre-order from €165.99 at Pokémon Center Germany up to €239.90 at French shops. The Elite Trainer Box has 9 packs and a Kyogre promo.

What to expect: the 30th Celebration showed how quickly launch prices fall. Its Futuristic Mew ex sold for around $1,260 on day one and is about €39 today. Unless you want a sealed display to keep, singles from Règne Delta will likely be cheaper in two to four weeks.

heading: 30th Celebration: the slide continues
body:
Six weeks after release, the anniversary set's special illustration rares are 13–20% below their 30-day averages: Mew ex 152 at €78, Gengar ex at €59, Pikachu ex at €47 and Mewtwo ex at €44. The three RGB Mew cards hold at €2,200–2,800 each and barely moved.

From Pitch Black (Nuit Noire), Mega Darkrai ex is holding up best at about €172. Mega Chandelure ex fell 18% this week.

In French, there is no 36-pack display for this set, only Elite Trainer Boxes, premium boxes and battle decks. That makes the French sealed products scarcer, which tends to help them hold their value.

heading: Heroines vol.2 is out, OP-18 is next
body:
EB-05 Heroines Edition vol.2 came out on 30 October in English and French (31 October in Japan). French boosters are already sold out at some big online shops, so it's worth asking the Réunion shops this week. The Nico Robin and Nami SP cards are the ones to look for.

OP-18 The Dominance of God follows on 20 November in English (21 November in Japan). French pre-release events run 21 to 28 November. The reported chase cards are a new God's Knights Super Parallel Gunko and Loki and Saint Shamrock parallels drawn by Yoshitaka Amano. Only Franky's card is officially confirmed so far.

French One Piece cards only exist from OP-09 onwards (the French line started in February 2025), so early French sets don't exist at all.

heading: Mihawk banned: what it means for prices
body:
Bandai banned the Green Mihawk leader (OP14-020) from 12 October, alternate arts included. Banned leaders usually lose most of their tournament value; collectors' alternate arts tend to hold up better because of the art.

The cards that gained from the ban are the ones players switched to: Loki alternate arts, Gloriosa and Black Luffy cards, and Green Shanks cards like Shanks OP17-022. In the first online events after the ban, Rocks D. Xebec was the most-played leader and Luffy & Ace won the most often. The Regionals in Porto and Sydney on Saturday will be the first real test.

heading: Championships: Dragapult rules, Nice went to a Basic Box
body:
Dragapult ex is the deck to beat, with 37% of top finishes this month, and it won Louisville and Puebla. Closer to home, the Nice Regional (17 October, 2,336 players) was won by Luc Gantner with an Ogerpon and Clefairy deck built around Mega Kangaskhan ex. A French player, Maxime Launay, came second with Dhelmise and Banette.

Next up: the Latin America International Championships in São Paulo on 20 November, then Stuttgart on 28 November. Cards in the winning decks often rise in the week after a big event, so Dragapult ex and Teal Mask Ogerpon ex are the ones to watch.

heading: Language gaps
body:
Pokémon: Japanese and English prices are close for the 30th Celebration chase cards. The Futuristic Mew ex is about $49 in Japanese and $46 in English. The bigger gap is on the Mega Rayquaza from the Japanese version of Règne Delta, which reached ¥298,000 (about $1,830) in July before falling. Watch how the English and French version prices compare once they open on Friday.

One Piece: the top card of OP-17, the Manga Rocks D. Xebec, sells for about ¥436,000 (about $2,830) in Japan but $6,100 in English. For the very top cards, English sells for far more than Japanese. For ordinary secret rares the two are about level.

heading: Your Réunion window: 55 days left
body:
Buying in shops on the island avoids the import costs that parcels from mainland France now carry (VAT, octroi de mer and La Poste's new €2 per item fee from 1 November). Miyata Kard Market in Saint-Louis is the only local site showing what's in stock; Sortilèges, Planet Geek and Mirage Island show prices and take pre-orders. PUNK Records in Le Tampon is the One Piece specialist.

When you fly home, personal items up to Rs 1,000 are allowed into Mauritius; above that, duty and 15% VAT can apply, so keep your receipts. The exchange rate is about Rs 53 to the euro.

heading: Coming up
body: 6 Nov: Pokémon Règne Delta (EN and FR). 7 Nov: One Piece Regionals in Porto and Sydney. 20 Nov: One Piece OP-18 (EN) and the Pokémon Latin America Internationals. 22 Nov: Pokémon Champions League Chiba. 27 Nov: Pokémon Aura Seeker in Japan, a preview of the February English set. 12–13 Dec: One Piece Regional in Paris and Treasure Cup in Rungis. 18–19 Dec: two new One Piece starter decks.

heading: About the numbers
body: Euro card prices come from Cardmarket's price guide, read through TCGdex and Limitless. Cardmarket pools all languages into one price, so a separate French price isn't available yet. One Piece box prices are eBay sales in US dollars. Dates marked unconfirmed in the calendar come from one news site, not from Pokémon or Bandai. This is the first edition, so week-on-week comparisons start next Monday.
